body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-24268","title":"Airworthiness Directives; GROB Aircraft AG Gliders","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/30/2026-24268/airworthiness-directives-grob-aircraft-ag-gliders","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all GROB Aircraft AG (GROB) Model GROB G 109 and GROB G 109B gliders. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of a fuel supply interruption that was caused by a cracked plastic fuel shut-off valve handle. This proposed AD would require repetitive inspections for cracks on a plastic fuel shut-off valve handle and replacement of the fuel shut-off valve with an improved fuel shut-off valve having an aluminum handle if any crack is found. This proposed AD also would prohibit the installation of a fuel shut-off valve having a plastic handle on any glider. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24227","title":"The Safer Affordable Fuel-Efficient (SAFE) Vehicles Rule III for Model Years 2022 to 2031 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks; Correction","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/30/2026-24227/the-safer-affordable-fuel-efficient-safe-vehicles-rule-iii-for-model-years-2022-to-2031-passenger","summary":"This document corrects technical errors in the final rule that appeared in the Federal Register on September 30, 2026, entitled \"The Safer Affordable Fuel-Efficient (SAFE) Vehicles Rule III for Model Years 2022 to 2031 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks.\" That document finalized amendments to fuel economy standards for light-duty vehicles for model years (MYs) 2022-2026 and MYs 2027-2031. The final rule also finalized amendments to compliance aspects of the program, including to vehicle classification and other compliance pathways.","publishedAt":"2026-11-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24216","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/30/2026-24216/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-11-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24215","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/30/2026-24215/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule establishes, amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPS) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure procedures (ODPs) for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-11-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24167","title":"National Advisory Committee on Travel and Tourism Infrastructure: Notice of Public Meeting","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/30/2026-24167/national-advisory-committee-on-travel-and-tourism-infrastructure-notice-of-public-meeting","summary":"This notice announces the meeting of the National Advisory Committee on Travel and Tourism Infrastructure (NACTTI or Committee). At the meeting, members will begin a discussion of the work they will undertake during their appointment term. Final agenda, registration, and any additional information for the meeting will be posted at least one week in advance of the meeting on the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT or Department) website at https:// www.transportation.gov/NACTTI.","publishedAt":"2026-11-30","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24140","title":"Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards: Automatic Emergency Braking Systems for Light Vehicles","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24140/federal-motor-vehicle-safety-standards-automatic-emergency-braking-systems-for-light-vehicles","summary":"NHTSA proposes to modify Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 127; Automatic emergency braking systems for light vehicles. NHTSA proposes to delay the compliance date by two years so that manufacturers have more time to comply with the standard. NHTSA also proposes test procedures for testing the malfunction telltale and to clarify the test speed tolerance. The agency seeks comment on other potential modifications to the standard.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24137","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (Type Certificate Previously Held by C Series Aircraft Limited Partnership (CSALP); Bombardier, Inc.) Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24137/airworthiness-directives-airbus-canada-limited-partnership-type-certificate-previously-held-by-c","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of engine stall events that occurred on ground in icing weather conditions (freezing fog) during engine acceleration to take-off thrust, or during the take-off phase. This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to provide the flightcrew with a prohibition to follow under certain freezing fog conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24123","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Request for Comments for a New Information Collection","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24123/agency-information-collection-activities-request-for-comments-for-a-new-information-collection","summary":"The FHWA has forwarded the information collection request described in this notice to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to approve a new information collection. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24122","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24122/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A330-202, A330-243, A330-243F, A330-302, A330-323, A330-343, A330-841, and A330-941 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by an investigation that revealed a potential discrepant gap between the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) vent intake panel and horizontal tail plane skin. This proposed AD would require modification of the NACA vent intake panel installation on the horizonal tail plane. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24120","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Bombardier, Inc., Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24120/airworthiness-directives-bombardier-inc-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model BD-700-1A10 and BD-700-1A11 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an issue with the heads-up display application (HDA) software in avionics software version 5.8 that could result in the HDA being unable to read errors in the graphical engine chip (GE5) local and frame buffer memory during power-up. This proposed AD would require installing avionics software version 5.9 or later approved software version. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24099","title":"Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24099/airworthiness-directives-general-electric-company-engines","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE90-110B1 and GE90- 115B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an aborted takeoff due to left engine failure caused by liberation of the interstage high-pressure turbine (HPT) rotor seal rim. This proposed AD would require determining the recalculated service life of the interstage HPT rotor seal and, depending on the results, replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal with a part eligible for installation. For certain engine populations, as an alternative to replacing the interstage HPT rotor seal, this proposed AD would require initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections of the interstage HPT rotor seal for cracks and, depending on the results, removing the interstage HPT rotor seal from service. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24096","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Experimental Permits for Reusable Suborbital Vehicles","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24096/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public to make public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The FAA collects information from applicants for experimental permits to determine whether they satisfy the requirements for obtaining an experimental permit.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24094","title":"Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for an Exemption From Liberty Bulk Transport, LLC, USDOT No. 3256390","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24094/parts-and-accessories-necessary-for-safe-operation-application-for-an-exemption-from-liberty-bulk","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to grant an application from Liberty Bulk Transport, LLC, USDOT No. 3256390, (Liberty) for an exemption to allow it to operate commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) equipped with a module manufactured by Intellistop, Inc. (Intellistop). The Intellistop module is designed to pulse the required rear clearance, identification, and brake lamps from a lower-level lighting intensity to a higher-level lighting intensity 4 times in 2 seconds when the brakes are applied and then return the lights to a steady- burning state while the brakes remain engaged. The Agency has determined that granting the exemption to Liberty would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety achieved by the regulation.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24088","title":"Hours of Service (HOS) of Drivers: Precision Fireworks LLC; Application for Exemption","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24088/hours-of-service-hos-of-drivers-precision-fireworks-llc-application-for-exemption","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to grant an exemption to Precision Fireworks LLC (Precision) (USDOT #3129980) during the designated Independence Day periods. The exemption allows drivers to exclude off-duty and sleeper berth time of any length from the calculation of the 14-hour limit. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and the public comments and has determined that the exemption, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24087","title":"Commercial Motor Vehicle Marking; Hours of Service of Drivers: Application for Exemption; Colorado Huntsman Transport, Inc.","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24087/commercial-motor-vehicle-marking-hours-of-service-of-drivers-application-for-exemption-colorado","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to deny the request from Colorado Huntsman Transport, Inc. dba Huntsman Transport, USDOT 4050798 (\"Huntsman\") for reconsideration of its application for exemptions from the commercial motor vehicle (CMV) marking requirements and the hours of service (HOS) 60 hour/7-day limit that the Agency denied on February 6, 2026. FMCSA analyzed Huntsman's application for reconsideration and the public comments received and has determined that the applicant did not provide information that would change the Agency's previous decision to deny the exemptions.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24086","title":"Hours of Service; Lone Star Haz Mat Response, LLC; Application for Exemption","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24086/hours-of-service-lone-star-haz-mat-response-llc-application-for-exemption","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to deny Lone Star Haz Mat Response, LLC's (Lone Star) application for an exemption to allow its \"field response\" drivers to exceed the hours of service (HOS) requirements for the purpose of returning to their normal work reporting location or residence following hazardous materials incident response operations. FMCSA analyzed the application and public comments and determined that the exemption would not likely achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24085","title":"Commercial Driver's License Standards: Application for Renewal of Exemption; National School Transportation Association","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24085/commercial-drivers-license-standards-application-for-renewal-of-exemption-national-school","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to renew the exemption granted to the National School Transportation Association (NSTA) for a period of two years to permit all commercial driver's license (CDL) applicants seeking a school bus endorsement to forgo the engine compartment portion of the pre-trip vehicle inspection skills testing requirement, known informally as the \"under-the-hood\" testing requirement. Drivers issued CDLs pursuant to the requested exemption are restricted to intrastate operation of school buses only. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and the public comments and has determined that the exemption, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24028","title":"Notice of Intent To Designate as Abandoned Felts Field Aviation Supplemental Type Certificate No. SA376NW","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24028/notice-of-intent-to-designate-as-abandoned-felts-field-aviation-supplemental-type-certificate-no","summary":"This notice announces the FAA's intent to designate Felts Field Aviation Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) as abandoned and make the related engineering data available upon request. The FAA has received a request to provide engineering data concerning this STC. The FAA has been unsuccessful in contacting Felts Field Aviation concerning the STC. This action is intended to enhance aviation safety.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24022","title":"Notice of Intent To Designate as Abandoned Martin Slone Supplemental Type Certificate Nos. SA441SW, SA500SW, SA501SW, SA512SW, and SA725SW","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/27/2026-24022/notice-of-intent-to-designate-as-abandoned-martin-slone-supplemental-type-certificate-nos-sa441sw","summary":"This notice announces the FAA's intent to designate Martin Slone Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) Nos. SA441SW, SA500SW, SA501SW, SA512SW, and SA725SW as abandoned and make the related engineering data available upon request. The FAA has received a request to provide engineering data concerning these STCs. The FAA has been unsuccessful in contacting Martin Slone concerning the STCs. This action is intended to enhance aviation safety.","publishedAt":"2026-11-27","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-24018","title":"Establishment of Class E Airspace; Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/25/2026-24018/establishment-of-class-e-airspace-trading-bay-production-airport-trading-bay-ak","summary":"This action establishes Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet above the surface at Trading Bay Production Airport, Trading Bay, AK. This action supports the safety and management of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at the airport.","publishedAt":"2026-11-25","source":"Federal Register"}]}
